exact_claim: Private foreign persons starting a non-national-security Australian business are not generally subject to mandatory FATA s 47 notification; the action is a reviewable national security action under FATA s 55E(2) (call-in / voluntary notification).
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; Commonwealth FATA; private non-FGI greenfield corporate presence
primary_source_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act 1975 (Cth)
what_source_establishes: Statutory pathways for starts an Australian business: private start-business is not a general notifiable action under s 47; s 55E(2) call-in residual applies when not otherwise significant/notifiable/NS-notifiable.
limitations_external_validity: Specialist legal review still required for deal structuring; FATR Part 3 exemptions not exhaustively mapped in Phase 0B.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: FGI pathway differs: FATR s 56(1)(b) makes FGI start-business significant and notifiable.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Primary legislation amending s 47/s 55E so private grocery start-business becomes generally notifiable, or published call-in practice showing routine screening of ordinary grocery greenfield starts.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as Layer A legal baseline for private greenfield corporate presence; do not treat as absence of all FDI friction.

exact_claim: Foreign government investors (FGIs) starting an Australian business is both a significant action and a notifiable action under FATR s 56(1)(b), using the FATA s 8B meaning.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; Commonwealth FATR; FGI greenfield start
primary_source_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Regulation 2015 (Cth)
what_source_establishes: FGI definition (s 17) and prescribed FGI actions including start-business notification (s 56(1)(b)); exceptions in s 56(3)–(7).
limitations_external_validity: FGI status is statutory; commercial intuition alone is insufficient.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Private Japanese-style retailer pathway is not interchangeable with FGI pathway.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Documented reclassification of a stylised private entrant as FGI under s 17 tracing rules.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible only when investor class is specified; bifurcation private vs FGI is mandatory.

exact_claim: Two related but distinct points for foreign vacant commercial land: (i) acquisition is generally notifiable at a $0 monetary threshold; (ii) Guidance Note 4 describes typical Treasurer productive-use conditions including commence continuous construction within about five years of purchase completion.
primary_source_title: Guidance Note 4 — Commercial Land (FIRB/Treasury); Monetary thresholds from 1 January 2026
source_date_or_version: Guidance Note 4 updated 2 Jan 2026; thresholds PDF from 1 Jan 2026
pinpoint: Guidance Note 4 §D typical conditions; vacant commercial $0 in thresholds summary PDF
what_source_establishes: Separates the notification trigger ($0 vacant commercial) from typical approval conditions (productive use / construction timing). Conditions are guidance describing usual practice not a freestanding statute and do not create a domestic incumbent release duty.
limitations_external_validity: Guidance is not the Act; conditions are case-by-case; thresholds PDF is an administrative summary.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Developed commercial land uses different (often high) monetary thresholds for certain FTA private investors.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Published practice showing vacant-commercial foreign approvals routinely without productive-use conditions, or statute creating identical domestic release duties.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as foreign vacant-land Layer A/B practice; treat notification trigger and typical conditions as distinct statements; not a general domestic land-banking remedy.

exact_claim: For private certain-FTA-partner investors (including Japan-formed private acquirers as listed), developed non-sensitive commercial land and non-sensitive entity substantial-interest thresholds from 1 Jan 2026 are more than $1,498 million (indexed summary).
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; private FTA-partner developed commercial land / entity acquisitions
primary_source_title: Monetary thresholds from 1 January 2026 (Treasury summary PDF)
pinpoint: FTA partner / developed commercial / entity tables
what_source_establishes: Administrative summary of indexed thresholds by investor class and asset type.
limitations_external_validity: Summary PDF; confirm against FATR before coding; eligibility depends on immediate acquirer jurisdiction.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: FGI land thresholds remain $0; vacant commercial remains $0 for all investors.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Annual indexation update or investor structuring that removes FTA eligibility.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible to show many store-level developed sites may fall below threshold for private FTA investors; not a guarantee of non-notification.

exact_claim: A lease or licence interest in Australian land arises under FATA s 12(1)(c) if the term including extensions/renewals is reasonably likely to exceed five years; agreements and options can bring forward acquisition timing under s 15.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; foreign leasehold / AFL / option interests
primary_source_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act 1975 (Cth)
what_source_establishes: Statutory land-interest and agreement/option acquisition rules.
limitations_external_validity: Deal-specific characterisation required for rolling renewals, licences, and conditionality under s 15(4)–(5).
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Short occupations may fall outside the s 12(1)(c) limb without eliminating other limbs or ACCC issues.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Authoritative ruling that a typical supermarket AFL with options is outside land-interest rules.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible for structure-specific FIRB branching; forbid modelling option = never regulated.

exact_claim: Major supermarket for targeted ACCC notification means Coles Group Limited, Woolworths Group Limited, and each connected entity only (Determination s 1-7); there is no market-share or revenue trigger in s 1-7.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; Competition and Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions) Determination 2025 Part 3
primary_source_title: Competition and Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions) Determination 2025
what_source_establishes: Closed-list definition of major supermarket.
limitations_external_validity: Foreign entrants do not become major supermarket by scale alone; expansion of class requires amending the Determination or becoming a connected entity.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: General Part 2 thresholds can still catch large foreign acquisitions.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Legislative amendment expanding s 1-7 beyond Coles/Woolworths connected entities.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as Layer A baseline for who faces Part 3 supermarket land/business notification.

exact_claim: From 1 Jan 2026, major supermarket acquisitions of supermarket businesses (s 3-1) and qualifying land interests meeting size tests (s 3-2: >1,000 m2 GLA building or >2,000 m2 without; adjacent aggregation; listed carve-outs) are notifiable regardless of general thresholds; Division sunsets under s 3-4 on 30 Jun 2030 unless remade.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; Coles/Woolworths connected-entity land and supermarket-business acquisitions
primary_source_title: Competition and Consumer (Notification of Acquisitions) Determination 2025
pinpoint: ss 3-1 to 3-4
what_source_establishes: Targeted notification classes and sunsetting.
limitations_external_validity: Notification is not prohibition; SLC still required for refusal; lease renewals/extensions and some ordinary-course land interests carved out.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Ordinary rivalry expansions may still be notified and assessed (Kalgoorlie pathway context).
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Remake/amendment of Part 3 before sunset; Tribunal/court narrowing of land-interest coverage.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as existing Layer A site-acquisition oversight for majors; PolisLab numeric caps/release rules remain additional.

exact_claim: If an ACCC notification waiver is granted, notification is not required for that acquisition even if thresholds apply; s 50 SLC prohibition still applies. If a waiver is refused, any applicable notification and standstill obligations remain in place; refusal is not itself a prohibition of the underlying acquisition.
primary_source_title: ACCC — Notification waivers
source_date_or_version: ACCC waiver page (aligned with Aug 2026 waiver guidance)
pinpoint: About notification waivers; consideration; consequence of non-grant
what_source_establishes: Institutional meaning of waiver vs notification determination; mandatory factors; grant removes need to notify; non-grant leaves notification pathway if thresholds apply; s 50 continues after grant.
limitations_external_validity: Guidance page summarises primary law; individual decisions are case-specific.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Pooling MN and WA outcomes into a single approval rate is invalid.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Statutory change equating waiver grant with substantive SLC clearance.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible only with MN/WA pathway separation; never treat waiver grant as proof of no competitive concern or as completed site control.

exact_claim: From 1 July 2026, a very large retailer (total covered revenue exceeding $30 billion for the previous financial year under Code s 8) must not engage in excessive pricing. Excessive pricing means, in all the circumstances, pricing that is significantly excessive compared with the cost of supply plus a reasonable margin (s 45B).
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; very large supermarket retailers under the Food and Grocery Code
primary_source_title: Competition and Consumer (Industry Codes—Food and Grocery) Regulations 2024 (Compilation as at 1 Jul 2026)
what_source_establishes: Covered-revenue threshold for very large retailer; conduct prohibition in s 45B(1); definition in s 45B(3) using in all the circumstances / significantly excessive / cost plus reasonable margin; record-keeping in s 45C.
limitations_external_validity: Establishes the legal conduct rule; measured effect on observed prices is not established in this product; not a fiscal rent levy; not a general price control for all grocers.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: PolisLab monopoly-rent levy remains a distinct Layer D instrument.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Enforcement precedents defining significantly excessive and reasonable margin under the in-all-the-circumstances test.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as post-1 Jul 2026 conduct-rule baseline for covered very large retailers; do not paraphrase as an empirical finding that high prices are constrained.

exact_claim: For 1 Apr–30 Jun 2026, Treasury reports that the median processing time for approved commercial investment proposals was 31 days, and that 50 per cent of those proposals were decided in 30 days or less. These are approval-cohort performance statistics, not statutory guarantees for every file.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; approved commercial FIRB proposals Q2 2026
primary_source_title: Quarterly report on foreign investment – 1 April to 30 June 2026
pinpoint: Headline statistics Median processing times; Chart 1 distribution bins
what_source_establishes: Median and share decided within 30 days for the approved commercial cohort that quarter; Chart 1 shows a distribution including longer processing-time bins.
limitations_external_validity: One quarter; approved-commercial cohort only; not supermarket-specific; does not prove that complex/NS/ACCC-overlapping files are excluded from the median calculation.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Does not establish approval probabilities by greenfield vs acquisition.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Multi-year distribution showing grocery/land files routinely take multi-year investment-screening delays as the binding constraint.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible to reject multi-year FIRB delay as a legal baseline median for approved commercial proposals; not admissible as a guaranteed clock for every file.

exact_claim: On 27 November 2025 Coles voluntarily notified (before mandatory notification commenced) a proposed leasehold acquisition of a vacant supermarket/liquor site in Kalgoorlie. On 30 June 2026 the ACCC determined the acquisition must not be put into effect. The ACCC's published reasons advance a prospective SLC theory that the acquisition would likely lead to exit of an effective independent full-line competitor and its assets.
primary_source_title: ACCC media release 1 Jul 2026; Phase 2 public Statement of Reasons 30 Jun 2026
source_date_or_version: Notification 27 Nov 2025; determination 30 Jun 2026; media 1 Jul 2026
pinpoint: Media release Merger control regime / Acquisition sections; Statement of Reasons public version (register PDF)
what_source_establishes: (1) Administrative refusal under the new regime after voluntary pre-commencement notification. (2) ACCC attribution of a prospective diversion/independent-exit theory of harm. Does not establish that independent exit occurred or that the theory is final law.
limitations_external_validity: Single local market; confidential evidence partly redacted; Tribunal review of the determination was on foot as of the official hearing listing through 19 Nov 2026; not a nationwide foreclosure finding; not a compulsory Part 3 notification example.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Competing explanation: short-run capacity/consumer gains dominate; independents not close substitutes; new entry offsets exit. Not classified as M1c land banking.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Final Tribunal orders/reasons affirming, setting aside, or varying the ACCC determination with published reasons.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as an administrative determination illustrating leasehold refusal power and as ACCC-attributed prospective SLC reasoning; not as an empirical finding that exit occurred; not as proof of compulsory Part 3 coverage for this deal; not as M1c foreclosure proof.

exact_claim: ACT 1 of 2026 is Coles' application for Tribunal review of the 30 June 2026 ACCC Kalgoorlie determination. The official Tribunal listing scheduled the substantive hearing for 9–12 and 16–19 November 2026. As of the release-pass retrieval of that listing, final Tribunal orders/reasons on the determination had not been located; a separate 24 September 2026 Tribunal determination concerns interim evidentiary issues under s 100S(2).
primary_source_title: Australian Competition Tribunal — Current matters listings; interim Determination 24 Sep 2026
source_date_or_version: Listing retrieved for Phase 0F release pass (21 Nov 2026); interim determination 24 Sep 2026
pinpoint: ACT 1 of 2026 hearing dates 9–12 and 16–19 Nov 2026; interim PDF Determination on s 100S(2) evidence applications
what_source_establishes: Official hearing schedule through 19 November 2026; existence of an interim evidentiary ruling. Does not by itself establish that a final merits decision was reserved or delivered.
limitations_external_validity: Listing pages are time-sensitive; secondary news reports of a reserved decision are not treated here as the official record of final disposition.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Pending review status is not contrary empirical evidence against the ACCC theory.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Publication of final Tribunal orders and reasons on the ACCC determination.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible only to date review status from the official listing and to distinguish interim evidentiary reasons from final merits reasons.

exact_claim: As at the ACCC Supermarkets Inquiry evidence base, undeveloped/unused sites intended for future supermarket use included ALDI 17, Coles 59 and Woolworths 105 (Coles+Woolworths combined 164). Freehold tends to be held longer than leasehold/AFL. Pipeline size is not proof of exclusionary intent.
primary_source_title: ACCC Supermarkets inquiry 2024–25 Final Report
pinpoint: Table 3.3 p 162; Figures 3.10–3.11; undeveloped-sites discussion pp 160–165
what_source_establishes: Descriptive pipeline counts by operator and interest type; holding-duration patterns; inquiry discussion of assessment limits.
limitations_external_validity: Compulsory-power descriptive inquiry; not a causal estimate; interest-type totals are pipeline facts.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Compatible with scarcity (M1a), planning (M1b), option value, and strategic foreclosure (M1c) — does not identify which dominates.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Parcel-level intent evidence showing nationwide purchase without intention to develop, or earlier than needed, to block rivals — or the reverse.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as descriptive O1/O2 pipeline fact; not admissible as proof of exclusionary land banking.

exact_claim: The ACCC inquiry explicitly did not determine case-by-case whether undeveloped sites constituted land banking (purchase without intention to develop, or earlier than needed, to block rivals); that assessment was outside inquiry scope.
primary_source_title: ACCC Supermarkets inquiry 2024–25 Final Report
pinpoint: Undeveloped sites / land-banking discussion pp 160–165 surrounding Table 3.3
what_source_establishes: Absence of a nationwide exclusionary land-banking finding — not a positive finding that foreclosure is absent.
limitations_external_validity: Inquiry design limits; confidential materials not fully public.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: UK CC likewise found controlled land can barrier entry locally while finding no systematic sole-purpose holding.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Future ACCC/court findings establishing (or rejecting) exclusionary holding in specific local markets.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as methodological caution: absence of finding is not proof of no foreclosure; keep CLAIM-M1c-1 live but unproven as general pattern.

exact_claim: ACCC inquiry finding: competitively effective chain entry requires suitable sites, supplier network, wholesale scale and capital; sites/planning emphasised; supplier network less significant; capital unlikely a significant barrier for large international entrants; ALDI took more than 20 years to current position.
primary_source_title: ACCC Supermarkets inquiry 2024–25 Final Report
pinpoint: Executive summary / retail competition barriers discussion
what_source_establishes: Authority ranking of candidate barriers for chain grocery entry; ALDI time-to-scale descriptive fact.
limitations_external_validity: Not peer-reviewed econometrics; not format-universal; does not estimate welfare from counterfactual entry.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Endogenous sunk costs and soft local rivalry remain competing concentration explanations.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Credible AU evidence that capital scarcity (not irreversible investment) blocked a large international grocery entrant with secured sites.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as AU descriptive barrier ranking and falsifying moment for capital-scarcity claims about large internationals; not as quantified barrier magnitudes.

exact_claim: ALDI is an important lower-price alternative in overlapping SKUs but a limited-range model that does not constrain majors on all dimensions.
primary_source_title: ACCC Supermarkets inquiry 2024–25 Final Report
pinpoint: ALDI competitive-constraint discussion
what_source_establishes: Format-contingent incomplete price constraint characterisation.
limitations_external_validity: Descriptive/regulatory assessment; not a diversion-ratio estimate.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Close-substitute low-price formats elsewhere can cut incumbent prices (HL2007; Basker) — conditional alternatives not automatic transfer.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU household-panel diversion ratios showing high full-basket diversion from majors to ALDI with broad incumbent price cuts.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible for CLAIM-M3b-1 and differentiated-format caution; do not infer O5 basket price discipline from ALDI store counts.

exact_claim: In ALDI's SA/WA expansion, contractor records show Regency Park (SA) contract completion in November 2015 ahead of early-2016 SA store rollout stocking, and Georgiou records the Jandakot (WA) DC as a late-2014 to early-2016 design-and-construct project supporting WA expansion. First SA stores opened 3 Feb 2016 and first WA stores 8 Jun 2016 (contemporaneous news). This is observed investment/opening order, not identification of a binding logistics constraint.
institutional_geographic_scope: South Australia and Western Australia; ALDI state network launch
primary_source_title: BADGE Regency Park project sheet; Georgiou Jandakot project page; contemporaneous opening reports compiled in Phase 0E
source_date_or_version: BADGE sheet (contract completion Nov 2015); Georgiou page (duration late 2014–early 2016); openings Feb/Jun 2016
pinpoint: BADGE: November 2015 contract completion and early-2016 rollout stocking note; Georgiou: Duration/Value; Phase 0E §3 for opening-day news citations
what_source_establishes: Contract-completion / project-duration facts for state DCs and independently reported first-store opening dates. Use contract completion for Regency Park unless a source establishes the date the DC became operational.
limitations_external_validity: Does not identify whether logistics, site assembly, or ordinary sequencing bound timing; H1 and H4 remain entangled under public evidence.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Ordinary investment sequencing (H4) is observationally compatible with the same DC-before-stores order.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Evidence of large sustainable SA/WA networks operating before local DC readiness.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as O2 chronology/moment only; not as a causal estimate that logistics bound SA/WA timing; not O5/O6.

exact_claim: ALDI's Making a good difference / Economic Impact Report (2018 figures) reports 29 South Australia stores, 41 Western Australia stores, and 526 stores nationally by end-2018.
institutional_geographic_scope: SA and WA; ALDI network aggregates
primary_source_title: ALDI Making a good difference — Economic Impact Report (May 2019; 2018 figures)
pinpoint: By the end of 2018… 526 stores; state pages listing 29 SA / 41 WA stores
what_source_establishes: Company-reported aggregate store counts by state and nationally for 2018.
limitations_external_validity: Company statistical report; not an independently audited census in PolisLab; survival observed but not the estimand.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Does not identify demand elasticities or incumbent price response.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Independent store-level census contradicting those aggregates.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as O2/O4 descriptive moment that frameworks must not contradict; forbidden as O5/O6 inference.

exact_claim: Phase 0C.2B identified nine Coles/Woolworths supermarket land/lease ACCC events under documented filters (acquirer party Coles or Woolworths; event date 1 Jul–30 Sep 2026; site land/lease inclusion rules). The sample mixes notification determinations and waiver decisions; anticipated openings are mostly 2027–2033; site-control completion and actual openings were coded not_independently_established. Selection rules and public register URLs are recorded in research/04_pilot_sample.csv and research/04_empirical_pilot_findings.md.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia; Coles/Woolworths land/lease events under documented Jul–Sep 2026 filters
primary_source_title: PolisLab Phase 0C.2B pilot findings and sample CSV (each row links an ACCC acquisitions-register URL)
source_date_or_version: Retrieval/coding 21 Nov 2026; event window 1 Jul–30 Sep 2026
pinpoint: research/04_empirical_pilot_findings.md §5–6 selection rules and table; research/04_pilot_sample.csv source_url column for MN-75042, WA-10038, WA-80043, WA-65037, MN-05046, WA-30035, WA-65032, MN-05030, MN-40034
what_source_establishes: Descriptive pathway mix and announcement horizons under stated filters; MN/WA must not be pooled; identified sample not a proven census.
limitations_external_validity: Project-scoped coding of public register pages; subsidiary/alt-name search not exhaustive; no deal-to-development link demonstrated for the nine events.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Waiver grant is not substantive approval; notification approval is not completed control or opening.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Independently verified completion/opening (or confirmed non-opening) for matured notified/waiver sites under pre-specified rules.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible to illustrate oversight process and realisation lag when accompanied by the pilot selection rules; not admissible as market-wide competitive-outcome evidence.

exact_claim: US Supercenter entry within about 1 mile associated with about 16% incumbent revenue drop with rapid distance decay; store-FE designs find no causal effect on incumbent prices despite large revenue diversion.
institutional_geographic_scope: United States; Walmart Supercenter / IRI supermarket panel
primary_source_title: Arcidiacono, Ellickson, Mela & Singleton (2020), AEJ: Applied
pinpoint: Abstract; distance-decay / store-FE price results
what_source_establishes: Credible reduced-form separation of revenue diversion from incumbent price response.
limitations_external_validity: US format/technology; mile radii not AU constants; few exits in sample.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Conditional alternatives: Hausman & Leibtag / Basker find price effects under different identification/formats.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU panel with store FE showing material causal incumbent basket price cuts after hard-discount entry.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as mechanism lesson (revenue is not price; localised effects); magnitudes not transferable as AU policy parameters.

exact_claim: Warehouse-club entry effects on incumbent grocery prices are format-contingent: Costco associated with higher incumbent prices; Sam's Club null; Supercenter studies elsewhere find price declines for some items.
institutional_geographic_scope: United States; warehouse clubs / ACCRA COLI
primary_source_title: Courtemanche & Carden (2014), Southern Economic Journal
pinpoint: Abstract / WP Costco estimates
what_source_establishes: Format-contingent incumbent price responses; contradicts universal entry⇒lower incumbent prices.
limitations_external_validity: US city panel; endogenous entry threat remains; ACCRA item mix.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: HL2007/Basker as conditional alternatives for close-substitute low-price entry.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU evidence that a differentiated foreign format systematically lowers major basket prices.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible to discipline format assumptions; not to assign Costco magnitudes to Australian specialty/hard-discount entrants.

exact_claim: UK planning regulation restricting large stores was associated with harm to independent retailers via chain shift into smaller, more central formats.
primary_source_title: Sadun (2015), Review of Economics and Statistics
pinpoint: Abstract / author PDF body
what_source_establishes: Adaptive response to large-format planning barriers; contrary to folklore that restricting large stores protects independents.
limitations_external_validity: UK PPG6 institutional context; employment is not consumer welfare; not AU planning schemes.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Does not negate planning as a candidate entry constraint (Griffith–Harmgart; Cheshire–Hilber–Kaplanis).
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU evidence that restrictive large-store rules raise independent employment/sales without chain small-format expansion into independent catchments.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as mechanism warning for site/planning rules; UK effect sizes not AU-portable.

exact_claim: UK Competition Commission (2008) found that combination of local concentration, planning, and controlled land can prevent/restrict/distort competition in highly concentrated local markets for larger grocery stores, while finding no systematic holding of land solely to create entry barriers.
primary_source_title: Competition Commission Groceries Market Investigation / Controlled Land Order materials
pinpoint: CAT Tesco [2009] CAT 6 ¶50–51 summary of CC findings; Order operative provisions
what_source_establishes: Official distinction between planning scarcity and controlled-land barriers; local AEC possible; absence of systematic sole-purpose holding.
limitations_external_validity: Pre-CMA; UK planning differs from Australian States; Order effectiveness not established in PolisLab register.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Supports CLAIM-M1c-1 as local possibility without proving AU nationwide foreclosure.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Credible public evaluation identifying CLO causal effects on AU-comparable entry/price/welfare outcomes.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as institutional comparator and competing-explanation discipline; not as proof that UK remedies would work in Australia.

exact_claim: Greenfield FDI and merger/acquisition FDI respond differently to barriers and policies and are not interchangeable modes.
primary_source_title: Davies, Desbordes & Ray (2018), Canadian Journal of Economics
pinpoint: Abstract / empirical mode-difference sections
what_source_establishes: Modes are distinct policy objects.
limitations_external_validity: Not Australian grocery-specific; does not directly estimate host grocery concentration effects.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Reviews show mixed host-country competition effects of foreign presence (Forte & Sarmento).
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU grocery designs showing foreign acquisitions systematically increase local fascia counts comparably to greenfield networks.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible to keep greenfield vs acquisition analytically separate; not to assert greenfield always wins on welfare.

exact_claim: More restrictive UK planning is associated with fewer large-format supermarket openings (Griffith & Harmgart). Separately, UK Town Centre First policy is associated with forcing stores onto less productive sites (Cheshire, Hilber & Kaplanis).
primary_source_title: Griffith & Harmgart (2012); Cheshire, Hilber & Kaplanis (2015)
source_date_or_version: Griffith & Harmgart IRRDC 2012; Cheshire et al. JEG 2015
pinpoint: Griffith & Harmgart abstract; Cheshire et al. DOI 10.1093/jeg/lbu007 (TCF productivity / output-loss discussion)
what_source_establishes: Two related UK planning findings: (i) restrictiveness reduces large-format store numbers; (ii) Town Centre First associated with less productive store locations. CHK companion URL: https://doi.org/10.1093/jeg/lbu007
limitations_external_validity: UK-specific institutions; structural assumptions; do not import £ or % magnitudes into AU models; Griffith abstract-level verification depth in Phase 0C.1.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Amenity/congestion benefits may offset consumer losses from fewer or relocated large stores.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: AU quasi-experimental planning-entry study with identified local effects.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as qualitative support for M1b; cite Griffith and CHK as distinct papers; magnitudes forbidden as AU parameters.

exact_claim: Post-2026 Australian baseline already includes transaction-specific FIRB pathways, mandatory ACCC merger notification (including Coles/Woolworths land/lease rules), Food and Grocery Code excessive-pricing for very large retailers, and typical foreign vacant-land development conditions — not a regulatory vacuum.
institutional_geographic_scope: Australia as at 20 Nov 2026 research cutoff
primary_source_title: PolisLab Phase 0B institutional baseline (synthesis of verified Layer A instruments)
pinpoint: Baseline §6 temporal layers / §9; Determination Part 3; Code ss 45A–45C; Guidance Note 4
what_source_establishes: Composite institutional characterisation synthesising verified Layer A instruments. Public anchors include the Determination compilation and related FIRB/Code sources cited in ATLAS-LEG rows.
limitations_external_validity: Project synthesis not economic effectiveness evidence; specialist legal review flagged in baseline.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Original MVP baseline that treated Australia as lacking site-control notification is corrected as unusable.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: Material repeal or non-commencement of Part 3 / Code excessive pricing / vacant-land condition practice.
admissibility_conditions: Admissible as framing baseline for all four cases; policy comparisons must be against post-2026 law, not a pre-reform caricature.

exact_claim: Logical chain O1→O2→O3→O4→O5→O6 is contingent at each step; access ≠ capacity ≠ viability ≠ survival ≠ durable constraint ≠ welfare.
institutional_geographic_scope: Analytical convention for PolisLab grocery assessments
primary_source_title: PolisLab Causal Mechanism Map — Phase 0C.1 (project synthesis)
pinpoint: Outcome definitions; logical relations; reinforced by AEMS2020 revenue≠price lesson
what_source_establishes: Outcome separation rules and conditional logical relations used throughout the casebook.
limitations_external_validity: Convention not an empirical estimate; map path is project-scoped.
competing_mechanism_or_contrary_evidence: Store-count or notification-count welfare folklore contradicts this convention.
observation_that_would_alter_assessment: A verified AU design showing automatic welfare gains from entry counts alone under stated conditions.
admissibility_conditions: Mandatory admissibility filter for all policy comparisons in this product.

exact_claim: Incumbents can deter rival entry by acquiring or leasing strategically important sites, holding options/AFLs, or using restrictive covenants/exclusivity, without timely productive use (CLAIM-M1c-1).
primary_source_title: UK Competition Commission groceries investigation (local controlled-land findings); ACCC inquiry pipeline without intent finding
pinpoint: CC controlled-land AEC findings; ACCC Table 3.3 / land-banking scope limit
